questions.q: Number of solutions of equations $\sin 9 \theta=\sin \theta$ in the interval $[0,2 \pi]$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Given, } \quad \sin 9 \theta=\sin \theta \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin 9 \theta-\sin \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos \left(\frac{9 \theta+\theta}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{9 \theta-\theta}{2}\right)=0 \\
& {\left[\because \sin C-\sin D=2 \cos \left(\frac{C+D}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{C-D}{2}\right)\right]} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos 5 \theta \sin 4 \theta=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \text{ Either } \cos 5 \theta=0 \text{$ or $} \sin 4 \theta=0 \text{, also } \theta \in[0,2 \pi] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 5 \theta=(2 n+1) \frac{\pi}{2} \\
& \text{ or } \quad 4 \theta=n \pi \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=(2 n+1) \frac{\pi}{10} \text{ or } \theta=\frac{n \pi}{4} \\
& \therefore \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{10}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{10}, \frac{9 \pi}{10}, \frac{11 \pi}{10}, \frac{13 \pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{17 \pi}{10}, \frac{19 \pi}{10} \\
& \text{ or } \quad 0, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \pi, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{4}, 2 \pi \\
& \therefore \text{ Total number of solutions }=17 \\
& \left(\because \frac{\pi}{2} \text{ and } \frac{3 \pi}{2} \text{ are common }\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The least positive non-integral solution of the equation $\sin \pi\left(x^{2}+x\right)=\sin \pi x^{2}$ is
options: irrational of the form $\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{p}}-1}{4},$ where $\mathrm{p}$ is an odd integer
irrational of the form $\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{p}}+1}{4},$ where $\mathrm{p}$ is an even integer
questions.solution: We have, $\sin \pi\left(x^{2}+x\right)=\sin \pi x^{2}\Rightarrow \quad \pi\left(\mathrmx^{2}+\mathrm{x}\right)=\mathrm{n} \pi+(-1)^{\mathrm{n}} \pi \mathrmx^{2}\therefore$ Either $\mathrmx^{2}+\mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{ m}+\mathrmx^{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{ m} \in \mathrm{I}$ or $\quad \mathrmx^{2}+\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{k}-\mathrmx^{2},$ where $\mathrm{k}$ is an odd integer $\Rightarrow \quad 2 \mathrmx^{2}+\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{k}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1+8 \mathrm{k}}}{4}$ For least positive non-integral solution is $x=\frac{1}{2},$ when $k=1$

questions.q: The number of real numbers $\lambda$ for which the equality $\dfrac{sin ( \lambda\alpha )}{sin\alpha} - \dfrac{cos ( \lambda\alpha )}{cos\alpha} = \lambda - 1$, holds for all real $\alpha$ which are not integral multiple of $\pi / 2$ is
questions.solution:
We have, $\dfrac{sin\left(\lambda\alpha\right)}{sin\alpha} - \dfrac{cos\left(\lambda\alpha\right)}{cos\alpha} = \lambda - 1$

$sin\left(\lambda\alpha\right)cos\alpha - cos\left(\lambda\alpha\right)sin\alpha = \left(\lambda - 1\right)sin\alphacos\alpha$

$sin\left(\lambda - 1\right)\alpha = \left(\lambda - 1\right)sin\alphacos\alpha$

$sin\left(\lambda - 1\right)\alpha = \dfrac{\lambda - 1}{2}sin2\alpha$

It is possible, when $\lambda - 1 = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 1$

and $\dfrac{\lambda - 1}{2} = 1 ⇒ \lambda = 3$

$∴ \lambda$ has only two solution.

questions.q: If $\tan (\cot x)=\cot (\tan x)$, then $\sin 2 x$ is equal to:
questions.solution: Given, $\tan (\cot x)=\cot (\tan x)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan x\right)\Rightarrow \cot x=n \pi+\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan x\Rightarrow \cot x+\tan x=n \pi+\frac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}=n \pi+\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sin 2 x}=\frac{n \pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{4}\Rightarrow \sin 2 x=\frac{1}{\frac{n \pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{4}{(2 n+1) \pi}$

questions.q: The general solution of the equation $\sin 2 x+2 \sin x+2 \cos x+1=0$ is
questions.solution: Given, $\sin 2 \mathrm{x}+2 \sin \mathrm{x}+2 \cos \mathrm{x}+1=0\Rightarrow 1+\sin 2 \mathrm{x}+2(\sin \mathrm{x}+\cos \mathrm{x})=0\Rightarrow(\sin x+\cos x)^{2}+2(\sin x+\cos x)=0\Rightarrow(\sin x+\cos x)(\sin x+\cos x+2)=0\therefore \sin x+\cos x=0$ or $\sin x+\cos x=-2$ But, $\sin x+\cos x=-2$ is inadmissible. Since, $|\sin x| \leq 1,|\cos x| \leq 1\therefore \sin x+\cos x=0 \Rightarrow \sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=0\Rightarrow x+\frac{\pi}{4}=n \pi \Rightarrow x=n \pi-\frac{\pi}{4}$
